I love how the very first page already frames the story as something special—notice the line “THE MILLENNIUM FULCRUM EDITION 3.0” right under the title [1]. It feels like a playful hint that this classic will be a pivot point for readers today. What do you think Carroll (or the editor) might be suggesting by calling this edition a “fulcrum” for the new millennium?
